full_judgment:
2. The plaintiff-respondent filed. Miscellaneous Case No.341 of 1979 under the Premises Rent Control Ordinance before the 1st Court of Munsif, Chandpur, acting as House Rent Controller. His case is that he is a tenant under the petitioner in respect of the case premises at a monthly rent of Tk. 200/- according to the English Calendar and that he has been paying rent regularly to the landlady (the predecessor-in-interest of the appellants) who has received the same upto month of October, 1979. Thereafter she has been refusing to receive the rent demanding unreasonable and unjustified enhancement of rent, so he sent rent of November and December, 1979 to her by postal money order who refused to receive it and, as such, the tenant-respondent filed the present case seeking permission to deposit the rent for the month of November and December, 1979. 

 3. The landlady, namely, the predecessor of the appellants, filed written objection contending inter alia that the plaintiff-respondent has no cause of action as she never refused to accept the rent; that on receipt of notice in the House Rent Control Case, she went to the tenant and asked him to pay rent to her and the plaintiff paid rent on 22-1-80 for the months of November and December, 1979 to her and assured that he would withdraw the case. But the plaintiff did not tender the rent for the months of January, and February, 1980 to her within the statutory period nor sent the same to her by money order. Further it was contended that the deposit of rent for the subsequent month from January 1980 and onwards was illegal under clause 19(1)(b) of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance and that deposit made without depositing the postal cost of transmission as provided under section 19(1)(b) of the Rent Control Ordinance was not a valid deposit and, as such, the House Rent Control case initiated by the tenant is not maintainable. 

 4. The learned Munsif rejected the land-lord's contention challenging the maintainability and held that "transmission cost as claimed by the O.P. (landlord) can be adjusted from the rent deposited and this matter will be decided at the time of final hearing". Against this order the landlady preferred Misc. Appeal No.290 of 1980 which was ultimately heard by the. learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Comilla, who by his judgment and order dated 9-9-1981 allowed the appeal and dismissed the plaintiff's case as not maintainable holding that as the tenant paid rent from the months of November and December, 1979 in cash to the landlady the tenant has no cause of action to proceed with a case and, as such, the tenant cannot legally deposit the rent of January 1980 and subsequent months without bringing any separate case on a separate cause of action. 

 6. Mr. Miah Abdul Gafur, learned Advocate-on-Record appearing on behalf of the appellant submits that the deposit of rent with the House Rent Controller admittedly without depositing the cost of transmission at any time is not a valid deposit under the Rent Control Ordinance 1963 and, as such, the tenant has no cause of action to proceed with the House Rent Case. Section 18 Sub-section (5) runs as follows:- 

 No tenant shall be entitled to the benefit of this section in respect of any premises unless, he pays the rent due by him in respect of such premises to the full extent allowable by this Ordinance within the time fixed in the contract with his landlord or, in the absence of such contract, by the fifteenth day of the month next following that for which the rents is payable, or in the case provided for in Section 19, unless the tenant has deposited such rent or any subsequent rent in respect  of such premises as provided in that section together with, in the case mentioned in clause (b) of sub-section (1) of that section, the cost of transmission referred to in that clause within the time specified in that section." 

 7. The underlined portion is relevant for our purpose. Section 19 Sub-section (1) Clause (b) provides that such rent required to be paid under Sub-section (5) of Section 18 is to be accompanied with cost of transmission by postal money order. Thus simple deposit of the amount of rent without depositing the cost of transmission by postal money orders cannot be considered to be a valid deposit and as such, the lower appellate court rightly held that the House Rent Control case initiated by the tenant-respondent in the circumstances stated above is not maintainable.
